AI agents

An agent for after launch

18 November 2026 · Reading time: 3 minutes

Google Labs has introduced Stitch Loop, an experimental product agent that connects to a codebase and live metrics, looks for what needs fixing and opens pull requests. Nothing merges until a person reviews it.

Sapaude retells the story in its own words. The source is below. Publisher: Sapaude.

In three points

Three points, in this order: what the source shows, where that claim stops, and what to check next.

  1. Teams connect GitHub plus logs, user behavior and feedback through more than 180 integrations, custom MCP servers or local CLI uploads.
  2. Each loop runs through four steps: suggestions, solutions, build in an isolated cloud sandbox with a GitHub pull request, and reflect, which keeps watching the metric.
  3. Built-in loops cover cybersecurity, latency and accessibility. The waitlist is open globally, with priority for eligible Google AI Ultra users.

The work after the merge

"Coding agents let you build and ship new features fast, but their job ends the moment your pull request merges," Google Labs writes. Once code is in production, the company argues, the real work starts: patching vulnerabilities, speeding up checkout and diagnosing signup drop-offs buried in noisy feedback. On November 18, 2026, Google Labs introduced Stitch Loop, which it calls a long-running product agent. It connects to a codebase and live metrics, finds what needs fixing and, according to Google, keeps working 24/7 until the goals are met.

Four steps per loop

Teams start by connecting GitHub and their product context, such as logs, user behavior and feedback, through more than 180 integrations, custom MCP servers or local CLI uploads. Stitch Loop then runs ongoing loops toward measurable goals. Each loop has four steps:

- Suggestions: opportunities to move toward the goal, grounded in evidence from the product. - Solutions: one or more options per suggestion, with tradeoffs, scoping and design options where relevant. - Build: once a team picks a direction, Stitch Loop writes the code in an isolated cloud sandbox and opens a GitHub pull request, with screenshots and videos where useful. - Reflect: the agent tracks live product data, learns from positive and negative results and keeps watching after the goal is met in case the metric slips.

"You always have the final call. Nothing merges until you review the PR," Google writes.

Security loop

Stitch Loop ships with loops for cybersecurity, latency and accessibility, and teams can add their own, such as improving checkout conversion. The security loop pairs Gemini 4 Carbon's security capabilities with CodeMender, Google DeepMind's autonomous agent for code security. Together they scan for vulnerabilities, flag each finding with evidence and open a pull request with a proposed fix.

Other coding agents, Google names its own Antigravity, can pull the same product context through the Stitch CLI and MCP. In Slack, @stitch sends daily insight digests and can start new loops.

Availability

The waitlist opened on November 18 for all users worldwide, with priority for eligible Google AI Ultra subscribers. Google's post gives no figures on findings, false positives or improvements in a real product.

What you can do

Stitch Loop aims at the work that starts after code ships. It is a waitlisted experiment, and Google's post shows no results from a real product yet.

In the app, the same story is also told shorter and in more detail, matched to your level.
